claim: UPSCRE displays player one’s score starting at PLYFLD+$1F — offset $01F decodes (offset = col*$20 + row, claim CW-11) to col 0, row $1F: the six score digits occupy columns 0-5 of the reserved top row.
UPSCRE enters the score with the carry SET (“ZERO SUPPRESSION”) — leading zeros of the first two digit pairs render as blanks until the first significant digit.
The last score pair is sent through DIGIT2 with the carry CLEAR (“NO ZERO SUPPRESSION”) — the final two digits always render, so score 0 shows “00”, never a fully blank field.
The high score displays at PLYFLD+$19F — offset $19F decodes to col 12, row $1F: six digits at columns 12-17 of the top row, drawn with the same SEC-then-CLC suppression.
DLIVES walks exactly six slots (“MAX NUMBER OF LIVES” = 6 into TEMP1) — a ship per remaining life, a blank per empty slot, six placements always.
Player one’s lives display at PLYFLD+$0DF — offset $0DF decodes to col 6, row $1F: the six life slots occupy columns 6-11, between the score and the high score.
The life icon is stamp $1F (“PICTURE OF SHIP”); an exhausted slot writes stamp 0, the blank.
DDTS2 is the routine that draws the DDT bombs onto the playfield, walking the DDTADD table.
The first bomb stamp written is DDT+1, at the entry address offset by Y=$20 — one column over from the entry’s own cell (claim HD-15 pins the $20).
The second bomb stamp written is DDT itself, at the entry’s own offset (Y EOR $20 back to 0) — so an intact bomb is the two-stamp pair DDT,DDT+1 across two adjacent columns of one row.
CHAR advances the screen address by ORA I,20 (with CKFF=0 upright) — +$20 per character, i.e. one COLUMN per character in the col*$20+row map: HUD text runs across columns of one row.
DIGITZ renders digit d as stamp $20+d (“DIGITS ARE 20-29”); the suppressed-zero path skips the ORA and writes A=0, the blank stamp.
UPSCRE is the routine that updates the scores on screen — the HUD’s score/high-score writer.
DLIVES is the routine that displays the lives — the HUD’s life-icon writer.
DDTS2 seeds Y=$20 for the upright picture order (cocktail flips it to 0) — the DDT pair’s second cell is one column (+$20) from the entry offset.
CHAR masks the advance with AND I,0E0 — the per-character step is exactly the $20 column stride, nothing finer.
